author: MELODY TUSCHEL
title: Small steps make a big difference - NewsBreak
text:
By MELODY TUSCHEL ,
7 hours ago Small steps make a big difference in the Keys.
Less is More:
• Choose products with less or better packaging. For example, buy a 32-ounce yogurt tub and put it into your own container instead of buying a 4-pack. Also, buy water in an aluminum bottle.
• Reusable is better than disposable. Choose washable glass containers, a refillable coffee mug (many cafés offer discounts), refillable water bottles and sturdy reusable shopping bags.
• Skip extra plastic. Fill coolers with ice at the machine and skip the bag
• Reusable shopping bags protect marine life and your purchase better, while avoiding petroleum-based plastics.
Reuse:
• Repurpose cereal and bread bags for pet waste, seafood prep scraps or other messy jobs.
• Reuse glass sauce jars for food storage, such as bacon grease you may want to use later, display a bouquet or store small hardware pieces.
• Recreate food leftovers. Turn last night’s hamburgers into today’s tacos, share with a neighbor or donate to the animal rescue when appropriate.
• If food isn’t edible, even for animals, compost food waste at home or at a food waste drop-off site.
• Visit makesoil.org to find the nearest food-scrap collection sites.
Recycle:
• Clamshells No. 1 PET (lettuce/berries/tomatoes).
• Clear No. 1 PET drinking cups or bottles.
• Dairy food containers (e.g., 32-ounce yogurt).
• Rigid plastics, such as detergent bottles, milk jugs, and peanut butter jars.
• Aluminum.
• Paperboard, old mail, paperback books, magazines and cardboard.
• Glass
Retail Drop-Offs:
• Publix – foam trays and egg cartons, film plastic bags, and clean storage bags
• Home Depot – rechargeable batteries, light bulbs and shopping bags
• Winn-Dixie – film shopping bags
Fighting Food Waste: Student Spotlight
Stanley Switlik Elementary School’s science department is back to worm composting with a 2,000-pound challenge this school year. Last school year, students spared 545 pounds of cafeteria fruit and veggie scraps from the dumpster. Red-wiggler worm bins in Mr. Sessler’s science class turn food scraps into snacks, The students used the finished compost to grow herbs and vegetables. They even enjoyed making cucumber pickles. Way to go, Dolphins!
Skip the Stuff:
• Monroe County, Key West and Islamorada have collaborated to only provide single-use items upon request (utensils, bags, straws, napkins, condiment packets).
• 40-plus businesses and 414 staff are acting against single-use waste.
Free Fall Tire Recycling Event:
Residents with IDs can recycle up to six passenger tires (no rims) for free from 8 a.m. to noon Friday, Oct. 4, at all Monroe County transfer stations. The tires are sent to American Tire Recycling to be crumbed and repurposed for road repairs and construction materials.
